flashcards.front_prompt: What challenge did Grandfather propose to Mario regarding his boast about having many friends?
flashcards.back_answer: Grandfather bet a bowl of fruit chaat that Mario did not have as many real friends as he claimed, introducing an invisible magic chair to test them.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Superficial popularity is very different from genuine friendship.

flashcards.front_prompt: What happened when Mario tried to sit on the invisible chair at school?
flashcards.back_answer: Mario missed the seat and fell flat on his back twice while his classmates laughed. On his third try, Guneet, Asma, and Deepa held him up in mid-air.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Fair-weather friends laugh at falls, while real friends step forward to support.

flashcards.front_prompt: What lesson did Mario learn from the invisible chair test?
flashcards.back_answer: Mario learned that out of dozens of classmates who laughed at his falls, only three were real friends who cared enough to catch him.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Quality of friendship matters far more than quantity of acquaintances.

flashcards.front_prompt: What is a suffix? Give examples from the chapter.
flashcards.back_answer: A suffix is a letter group added after a root word to alter its meaning (e.g., 'friend' + '-ship' = friendship, 'boast' + '-ful' = boastful).
flashcards.key_takeaway: Suffixes transform root words into new parts of speech.
